## Development data science

Ongoing independent projects applying modern ML to core development-economics measurement problems, with a focus on African contexts.

### Poverty estimation from satellite imagery

Training convolutional neural networks on satellite imagery, calibrated against household-survey data, to produce small-area estimates of poverty and wealth indicators in regions where survey coverage is sparse or infrequent. The goal is timely, low-cost poverty maps that complement (not replace) traditional survey programs.

### School and hospital mapping

Detecting and mapping schools and health facilities from satellite imagery to support service-delivery planning and equitable resource allocation, particularly where official facility registries are incomplete or outdated.

### Informal cross-border trade

Informal cross-border trade is a large but poorly measured share of intra-African commerce. I am working on model-based estimation strategies that combine limited field observation with auxiliary data to produce credible ICBT estimates, a problem where careful survey design and statistical modeling matter as much as the data collection itself.

## Medical machine learning

### Offline reinforcement learning for sepsis treatment

Using the **MIMIC-IV** critical-care database to study offline (batch) reinforcement learning for sepsis treatment policies: learning from retrospective ICU trajectories, with emphasis on reliable off-policy evaluation, so that learned policies can be assessed honestly before any claim of clinical relevance.

---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
These projects share a common thread with my [methodological research](research.qmd): when data are expensive (surveys, field studies, clinical records), experimental design and sample-efficient optimization decide what is learnable.
:::
